name: Slow Week at the Old Sanatorium
summary: A free week for up to 70 people at a former sanatorium run by a secular foundation. Two optional daily sits, silent mornings, and nothing else asked. Made for the exhausted. Beginners.
description:
The foundation runs the Slow Week twelve times a year, at no charge, for people who need a week of not doing anything.

**What happens**
Very little. A sit at 7:30 and at 17:30, each 30 minutes, guided by a member of staff, both optional. Mornings are silent throughout the building and grounds until noon. Meals at fixed times. That is the whole structure.

**Staff**
Three staff live in during each week. They are trained in secular mindfulness and are available for a conversation any afternoon; there is a sign-up sheet. They do not teach unless asked.

**Physical**
Nothing. The grounds are level, the porches are long, and sleeping is encouraged. Many guests sleep twelve hours a night for the first three days.

**For whom**
Anyone, and especially people who have never done anything contemplative and would not call this that. About 70 guests a week.

**Cost**
None. The foundation was endowed for this purpose.
practical: Saturday to Saturday, monthly. Free. Up to 70 in shared rooms (two to four beds). Three simple meals. Bring slippers, warm clothing, a book. Level access throughout. Nearest bus Saranac Lake; the foundation van meets the afternoon bus. Wifi in the office only; guests are asked to leave phones in their rooms.
